Conflict: Material and Design Agent and Circularity Agent recommend monomaterial recycled plastics; In-Service Agent and Manufacture Agent reject this because they require thick virgin ABS/PC or metal to ensure impact durability and prevent microplastic release.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Monomaterial unpainted plastics (e.g., pure polypropylene) with optimized structural ribbing
Rationale: Monomaterial unpainted polypropylene complies with ESPR Annex I (d) for high-purity recycling and Annex I (t) for lightweighting, while structural ribbing ensures compliance with Annex I (a) durability without needing heavy metal or thick virgin ABS/PC.

Conflict: Material and Design Agent and Circularity Agent recommend snap-fits and standardized screws; Manufacture Agent and In-Service Agent reject this because snap-fits can break during repeated repairs and increase assembly complexity.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Rationale: Reversible fasteners facilitate easy disassembly and re-assembly, which is crucial for the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (Parameter c, Page 27, 79). This choice directly avoids technical solutions detrimental to end-of-life recovery (Parameter e, Page 79) and ensures components can be separated cleanly to maximize recycling quality (Parameter d, Page 79) while minimizing waste generation (Parameter r, Page 80).

Conflict: Material and Design Agent and Manufacture Agent recommend a brushed DC motor for simpler manufacturing and recycling; In-Service Agent and Circularity Agent reject this because brushed motors have lower energy efficiency and shorter lifespans than brushless alternatives.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Modular brushless DC motor with mechanically secured, easily separable magnets
Rationale: A brushless DC motor significantly improves energy efficiency (parameter g, Page 79) and durability (parameter a, Page 79). To satisfy Circularity and Material and Design's recycling concerns, the BLDC motor must use mechanically secured, non-glued magnets to allow easy separation of rare-earth elements at end-of-life, satisfying Annex I (d) and (e).

Conflict: Material and Design Agent and Manufacture Agent recommend passive cooling to minimize weight and complexity; In-Service Agent rejects this because passive cooling leads to higher operating temperatures that degrade motor durability.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Passive cooling via structural ventilation slots and lightweight aluminum heat sinks
Rationale: A dedicated active cooling fan increases spatial volume, weight, and material footprint, which conflicts with lightweight design (Annex I (t), Page 80) and increases resource consumption. Passive cooling, combined with a modular, high-efficiency BLDC motor (which generates less heat), is engineering-feasible and satisfies Annex I (t) and (f) by avoiding complex active components and substances of concern (like potted compounds).

Conflict: Material and Design Agent, In-Service Agent, and Circularity Agent recommend a highly modular architecture for repairability; Manufacture Agent rejects this because modularity increases manufacturing complexity, resources, and production waste.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Highly modular architecture with standardized, swappable sub-assemblies and clear material coding
Rationale: Regulatory compliance with ESPR Annex I (b) ease of repair and maintenance (Page 79) and (c) ease of upgrading/remanufacturing (Page 79) is non-negotiable. A monolithic design would lead to premature obsolescence when a single component fails, directly violating the ESPR's core circularity mandates.

Conflict: Material and Design Agent, Manufacture Agent, and In-Service Agent recommend a mains-powered corded design; Circularity Agent rejects this because cordless designs with user-replaceable batteries provide superior user mobility and circular battery recycling streams.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Mains-powered corded design with integrated cord reel and no chemical battery
Rationale: Eliminating the battery completely avoids the use of substances of concern (Annex I (f), Page 9), prevents hazardous waste generation (Annex I (r), Page 80), and avoids battery degradation which limits the product's technical lifetime (Annex I (a), Page 79). While cordless offers convenience, a corded design ensures consistent functional performance (Annex I (s)) and significantly reduces the product's lifecycle environmental and carbon footprint (Annex I (m), (n)).
